summary: The patch fixes the reported skipped-test symptom but does so by discarding the `_explicit_tearDown` deferral mechanism and inspecting unittest's private `_outcome.skipped`, which changes when tearDown runs under --pdb and over-suppresses runtime skips. The established idiomatic fix is to guard the existing swap with `not _is_skipped(self.obj)` (checking `__unittest_skip__`); this rewrite is fragile and regression-prone.

issues.description: Removes `self._explicit_tearDown = self._testcase.tearDown` and the no-op swap entirely. That deferral was deliberately introduced so that under --pdb tearDown runs in pytest's teardown phase (after the debugger enters), not inline. With the wrapper, tearDown executes during unittest's normal run() again (and pytest's teardown() never calls `_explicit_tearDown`, which stays None), reintroducing pre-fix timing for failing tests under --pdb. Approach also leans on the undocumented internal `_outcome` attribute (the hasattr guard signals uncertainty it even exists).

`_outcome.skipped` is broader than `__unittest_skip__`: for a runtime `self.skipTest()` in the test body, plain unittest still runs tearDown (setUp succeeded), but this wrapper suppresses tearDown only under --pdb. That diverges --pdb behavior from non-pdb behavior for runtime skips.

Reinvents skip detection via the private `_outcome.skipped` list instead of the project-idiomatic `getattr(obj, '__unittest_skip__', False)` check on `self.obj`; also mixes a nested closure and quoted attribute name where the codebase favors the simpler guarded-swap pattern.
